study: Arens et al. 2012 (OWE curriculum + RISE PD, REL Central, NCEE 2012-4013)
eval_evidence: REL Central / McREL conducted the IES-funded NCEE evaluation; OWE and RISE are commercial products (Rigby / Harcourt Achieve), so evaluators have no developer stake. Conflict-of-interest disclosure is the standard IES contractor notice.
developer_evidence: 'Most teachers in the intervention group received their RISE training from a publisher-trained site coordinator rather than directly from the publisher.'
cascade_evidence: Train-the-trainer cascade: the publisher trained site coordinators, who in turn trained most teachers (publisher -> site coordinator -> teacher, >=1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Control group received business-as-usual ESL instruction.
coaching_evidence: RISE delivered mainly as eight two-hour workshops over one school year (professional-consultant model) with facilitator instructional demonstrations and some coaching; no documented recurring monthly+ in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: OWE is a teacher-delivered ELL curriculum used during regular ESL instruction (>=30 min/day); it changes what the teacher teaches rather than adding a separate tutoring/pull-out/extra-minutes student dose. (An extra OWE oral-language strand was supplied but is still teacher-delivered in regular time.)
maturity_evidence: Year 1 (2008/09) was training/baseline; Year 2 (2009/10) was the first implementation year, when OWE+RISE were used and the spring-2010 outcome was measured -- the program's first implementation year.
